rationale: Engineering teams at AI-adopting companies (5–200 engineers) with existing Claude Code or Cursor subscriptions face a real, recurring structural pain every time an agent touches a test file — this is a credible B2B buyer with demonstrated software-tool budgets. However, buildability sits at the moderate level because a policy/governance layer that correctly scopes agent access to test files requires non-trivial CI/CD integration (GitHub Actions, repo hooks, possibly IDE plugins), and the product form is not yet clear enough to ship as a prompt + landing page alone. The willingness_to_pay signal is decent — these teams already pay per-seat for coding agents — but no direct pricing probe or comparable product validates the specific test-governance niche yet, so the operational_autonomy floor of 7 is not quite met (integration work per customer is likely needed). Validate the form factor (SaaS policy layer vs. open-source tool vs. managed service) and get five engineering leads to describe what they'd actually pay for before committing to build.
solution_plan: WHAT: A SaaS policy layer ('TestGuard') that sits between an AI coding agent and a repo's test files, reviewing proposed test mutations and either gating them for human approval or auto-classifying them as safe/risky based on configurable rules. BUILD: The factory sets up a Claude-powered review prompt that evaluates a git diff touching test files, classifies changes (new test, modified assertion, deleted coverage, etc.), and returns a risk verdict; this is wired to a webhook that integrates with GitHub/GitLab via a simple OAuth app — the operator approves the app registration, then the factory manages all configuration files and documentation. A Stripe-linked pricing page and self-serve onboarding form are generated by the factory with no coding by Youval. SELL: Outreach targets engineering leads and DevOps managers at Series A–B startups already paying for Claude Code or Cursor, reached via LinkedIn (job titles + company size filter) and HN 'Who's Hiring' threads; the factory drafts and queues each outreach batch, Youval approves before sending. MAINTAIN: Once a team connects their repo, the webhook runs automatically, Claude evaluates every agent-generated test-file PR, verdicts are posted as PR comments, and billing runs via Stripe; Youval's only recurring touch is approving outreach batches and monitoring the weekly summary. CAVEAT: The CI/CD integration step (setting up the GitHub App, handling webhook auth, managing repo permissions) is moderately complex and may require a one-time external contractor to build the connector properly before the factory can maintain it — Youval should factor this in before committing.
notes: operational_autonomy scored 6 — just below the build_gate floor of 7 — because initial customer onboarding likely requires per-repo configuration help until a fully self-serve connector is built. Stage capped at validate until a self-serve integration path is confirmed.
